findings.description: The user_data script exports static AWS access key and secret access key values in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process on the host or via SSRF, and is also persisted unencrypted in Terraform state and the EC2 API, leaking long-lived IAM credentials.

No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. On an internet-facing web server this makes SSRF-based retrieval of instance metadata (including the credentials embedded in user_data) trivial.

The instance sits in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true, routed to an internet gateway, and is attached to a security group permitting 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 22 and 80, so it is directly reachable from the internet with no bastion, load balancer, or NAT boundary.

No root_block_device encryption is specified, so unless the AMI or account-level EBS default encryption enforces it, the root volume - which will contain the user_data-derived environment and any application data - is stored unencrypted.
The ingress rule allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling credential brute-force and exploitation attempts against the host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user_data provisions a plain Apache HTTP listener with no TLS anywhere in the configuration, so all traffic to the host travels unencrypted.
Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, placing no outbound restriction on a compromised host and easing data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic.
The volume does not set encrypted = true (the attribute is deliberately commented out), so data written to the volume attached to the web host is stored unencrypted and unprotected by KMS.

The snapshot is derived from the unencrypted aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage and therefore inherits no encryption, creating a persistent unencrypted copy of the volume data that can be copied or shared across accounts.

The VPC flow log bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, so network traffic metadata (source/destination addresses, ports, accept/reject decisions) is stored without enforced encryption at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, removing the defence-in-depth control that prevents a later ACL or policy change from exposing network logs publicly.
The bucket has no policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so log data may be written or read over unencrypted HTTP connections.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true, combined with the route table association routing 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway, gives every instance launched here a routable public IP by default, eliminating network segmentation for the workload tier.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the internet-gateway-routed table make any instance launched in this subnet internet-facing by default.
